newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court leaves in place Dutch booksellers' pricing scheme.
newsitem.headline: Court leaves in place Dutch booksellers' pricing scheme.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday that restrictive book pricing schemes in the Netherlands can remain in force if they were agreed before Community rules on competition were implemented.
The Dutch booksellers' union (KVB) challenged the Free Record Shop's twenty-five percent discount on selected book titles, claiming the sale violated the union's pricing rules.
KVB members are required to maintain a system of imposed retail prices, even with regard to non-members such as the Free Record Shop, according to court documents.
The Free Record Shop challenged the agreement under EC treaty rules on competition, but KVB maintained its rules enjoy provisional validity.

In a reference for a preliminary ruling, the European Court ruled restrictive sale agreements agreed before 1962 remain provisionally in force if they were notified to the European Commission and the Commission took neither a positive or negative decision on the agreement.
However, if the terms of restrictive sales agreements have been altered in any way, except to make them less restrictive, they are considered void.

"It is settled-case law that agreements concluded after the entry into force of (Community law on competition) that are merely a replica of a standard contract concluded previously and duly notified, benefit from the same system of provisional validity as the latter contract," the court said.
"Any introduction of new restrictions must...be regarded as having brought to an end the old agreement...and as introducing a new agreement which does not enjoy provisional validity."
Reference from the Arrondismentsrechtbank te Amsterdam in the case between
Koninklijke Vereeniging ter Bevordering van de Belangen des Boekhandels
Free Record Shop BV, Free Record Shop Holding NV

on the interpretation of article 85 of the EC treaty and of Council regulation No 17 of 6 February 1962, First regulation implementing articles 85 and 86 of the treaty (OJ, English Special Edition 1959-1962, p. 87), as amended by Council regulation No 59 of 3 July 1962 (OJ, English Special Edition 1959-1962, p. 249)

1. The provisional liability of a restrictive agreement which was concluded before the entry into force of Council regulation No 17 of 6 February 1962, First regulation implementing articles 85 and 86 of the treaty, as amended by Council regulation No 59 of 3 July 1962 and which was notified to the Commission before 1 November 1962 expires only when the Commission has taken either a positve or a negative decision on that agreement.

2. A duly notified restrictive agreement concluded before the entry into force of regulation No 17, as amended by Council regulation No 59, enjoys a provisional validity only if its terms remain unchagned or, in the event of amendments, if these do not have the effect of reinforcing or extending its restrictive efffects.
